scope: Narration is the spoken > lines of s5_ai/script.md (8 scenes; text unchanged since the earlier 2026-10-23 review), with s4_analytics/script.md as the also story, where evidence caps a verdict at partial. Screen verdicts are judged on the 8 scenes of s5_ai/deck_anim.html and the eight qlik_panels/*.png they embed, each opened and looked at, and on frames pulled from the finished 05_MCG_AI_Outcomes_1080p.mp4 (3:31, re-cut 2026-10-23 21:08 from the 21:04 s5_ai build). In this cut narration lines 2-8 each start about half a second after their own slide; line 1 does not: the title slide and its Predict panel are up for 0.4 s (3.0-3.4 s) straight after the opening sting, and 'Story four of four' plays over the empty 'Build side, consumption side' heading. The closing slide holds until the last word (about 204 s) and hands to the end sting at 206 s.
note: Ingrid, the re-cut fixes the timing, not the substance: the narration is word for word what I failed earlier today, and so is my verdict. The build-side loop is sound - 'the human owns the decision' and 'it is a git revert' are sentences I would put in front of the NVWA - but preview is never said aloud, the Discovery Agent's alert reaches no named person, nothing on the consumption side has an approver, and no AI system is ever shown acting on our tenant. The one live machine-learning screen is up for less than half a second, before anyone speaks, and it reads 'No features were selected for bias detection'. Six of the seven musts are open; this pillar is not ready to show.

verdicts.evidence: The closing panel shows the Supply Chain Health data product on the live tenant with its Description labelled 'Generated by AI on October 23, 2026 at 6:45 PM', a Qlik Trust Score of 3.8/5 and owner Robert Schoenfeld; it is on screen from 183.6 s to 206 s. The small-print AI label is the only AI output a viewer has time to see.
verdicts.gap: No scene shows an AI system at work on the tenant: no Answers response with its citation, no agent conversation, no Discovery Agent configuration, no coding-agent session. The other AI surface, the Qlik Predict experiment on sc1 (v5_predict_coldchain.png, also used by the analytics video), is on screen for 0.4 s straight after the sting and before the first word, and it reads 'No features were selected for bias detection' with a best-model F1 of 0.144. The sc3 diff and 'Problems: 0' chain are drawn HTML over v2_pipelines.png, two project cards (MCG Supply Chain Pipeline, olh_mcg_demo_cdc), neither of them the mcg-batch-pipeline the code header names. sc4's 'What the Discovery Agent watches' is v3_dataquality.png, Qlik's stock semantic types (Name suffix, AT VAT Number..., all created by Qlik on Jul 29, 2025) with nothing on freshness, thresholds or MCG datasets. sc6's agentic route sits on v2_connections.png, a list of three source connections. The AI-generated description on sc8 shows no reviewer.

verdicts.evidence: It cites the NinjaVan contract amendment, effective the first of October
verdicts.gap: Video 05 never says that an answer cites a source. All it says about Answers is 'Ask a question, get an answer', with a pointer back to story three, so a viewer of this video alone hears about AI answering questions with no citation at all. The NinjaVan example exists only in the analytics narration, and none of the eight panels here is an Answers response: v4_answers.png exists in qlik_panels but this deck does not embed it.

verdicts.evidence: through the Qlik MCP server — an assistant calling live Qlik tools to create the sheet
verdicts.gap: The AI video never mentions MCP. In the analytics video the Qlik MCP server is only the channel one assistant used to author sheets. Nobody says that any MCP-compatible assistant, not only Qlik's, can reach the governed data products, quality metrics, lineage and catalog, or that permissions, trust scores and draft status travel with them. The interoperability claim that stops this reading as a closed vendor stack is never made.

verdicts.evidence: trust score falling below zero point seven, sync lag over an hour, volume moving more than fifty percent
verdicts.gap: The thresholds land; the recipient does not. 'Seventy-two silent hours becomes an alert', but no product owner, steward, channel or role is named as its reader, so the alert has no accountable person. 'Can watch' leaves open whether the agent is actually configured on these two products, and the sc4 panel shows no agent configuration. The 0.7 threshold is on a different scale from the Trust Score the closing panel shows (3.8 / 5), so a viewer cannot tell what would trip it.

verdicts.evidence: Generated terms arrive in draft status and wait for a human to approve them.
verdicts.gap: Gates are named for three build-side actions: the coding agent ('The human owns the decision'), glossary drafts, and low-confidence addresses ('to a human steward'). No approver is named for the Data Product Agent packaging products, the Data Quality Agent turning a sentence into an enforced rule, the Discovery Agent's alert, or the automations: 'except the one step that should stay human' never says which step, or whose. Nothing is gated on the consumption side; in the analytics video a sentence of plain English 'can end up as a governed object in a governed app' with no reviewer. Every approver is 'a human' or a steward, never a role with sign-off authority. On screen, sc5's glossary shows every visible term in Draft with the Stewards column empty, and sc8's AI-generated description carries no review.

Neither the AI nor the analytics narration says the word 'preview'. Declarative pipelines ('just YAML in a git repository'), the agentic route and sheet authoring over the Qlik MCP server are all presented as working capability. The only preview label is the sc6 footer 'Preview / roadmap', small print the criterion excludes. The one honesty line that is spoken, 'Qlik Answers capabilities, not separate products', is about packaging, not release status.

verdicts.evidence: And the model can run in your own tenant.
verdicts.gap: Said once, for the address route only, and as an option ('can run'), not as how Meridian runs it. Nothing says where customer data goes: the quoted 'the language model never leaves our infrastructure' is about the model, not the data, and is framed as what a buyer wants to hear. A Qlik Cloud tenant is hosted by Qlik, so 'your own tenant' and 'our infrastructure' are not the same thing, and the narration blurs them. Nothing says where the coding agent, the governance agents or Answers send prompts and data.

verdicts.evidence: the build side produces trust, and the consumption side spends it.
verdicts.gap: A slogan, not a demonstration. The two gold products are tied only to the agents ('what the agents operate on'); no consumption surface in this video is shown or said to read Supply Chain Health or Last Mile Performance. The one worked Answers example, in the analytics video, reads twenty-five operational documents, not the gold products. A viewer is told that trust is spent but never who spends it, or on which product.

verdicts.evidence: The agent does the typing. The schema catches the mistakes. The human owns the decision. And if it is wrong, it is a git revert.
verdicts.gap: The narration is complete. On screen, the YAML diff and the schema check are drawn rather than captured, over two project cards that are not the mcg-batch-pipeline the code header names. The repo's MCG CRM Landing schedule.yaml still reads INTERVAL=15 ('every 15 minutes'), so there is no commit of the 30-minute change and no record of who approved it.
